items.title: Butch Miles interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 9, 2020 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: I could understand it if it was, you know, a Lester Young recording.

ctx.x: And I think they had some new microphones, some omni-directional microphones I think, that they set up on the stage instead of having mics on each and every instrument you know, and overhanging the drums and on the bass and the snare and stuff. They had one or two or three microphones set up to catch the live effects of the auditorium, the theater that we were playing in. So the sound is different.

Yes, they got it. So I’ve had a couple of circumstances recently where I’ll make a reference to a student, let’s say I might say something like, “You know that Weather Report ‘Birdland’ wonderful recording —” and they’ll look at me like with this blank thing. And I’ll go oh no, don’t tell me. And I could understand it if it was, you know, a Lester Young recording. But I’m wondering if this has happened to you.

Yes. The older I get, the more I teach, the younger the students and the more blank stares I get sometimes when I do exactly what you just did. I suggest a recording, a specific recording from 20, 30, 40, 50 years ago, and it’s sort of like I might as well be talking about Fred Flintstone and his band back in Bedrock, or whatever. They’ve got no idea. But then, in all fairness Monk, they’ll look at me and they’ll talk about, “Have you heard the latest from” so-and-so. And I don’t have any idea who they’re talking…
